    <item>
      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/d668e44ea9f6f3fb2d88cfee76bb772cccada10f/456_0_4053_3243/master/4053.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=7839a06430930a2378822738556852d7">

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 21:53:35 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Business</category><title>Rogue AI: California sues OpenAI over "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/business/20261116-rogue-ai-california-sues-openai-over-hugging-face-and-other-cyberattacks</link><description>
The US state of California has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI over the "Hugging Face" and other cyberattacks, accusing the ChatGPT maker of knowingly testing dangerous advanced AI models without adequate safeguard. Meanwhile, the US Commerce Department has tightened rules over the export of US technology, aiming to close a loophole around remote access to advanced AI chips. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6ceddd6e-e201-11f1-a43b-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-NW-IVS-ECO-CALIFORNIA-STATEMENT-OPENAI-LAWSUIT-ROYER-Yuka-transfer.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/6ceddd6e-e201-11f1-a43b-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-NW-IVS-ECO-CALIFORNIA-STATEMENT-OPENAI-LAWSUIT-ROYER-Yuka-transfer.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fd2e098a-e201-11f1-893e-93310cbf72bd</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 21:27:15 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Yuka ROYER</dc:creator></item><item><category>Eye on Africa</category><title>Rwanda to host hub for rejected EU migrants</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/rwanda-to-host-hub-for-rejected-eu-migrants</link><description>
In tonight's edition, five European countries are negotiating a deal to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. Also, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda's political animosity spills over at the Francophonie Summit in Cambodia. And in Tunisia, young women are increasingly turning towards weightlifting and bodybuilding as a form of self-expression.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3919d2d0-e202-11f1-8e3c-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/DL00006253-VOD-00023667.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3919d2d0-e202-11f1-8e3c-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/DL00006253-VOD-00023667.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4854abbc-e202-11f1-a03e-fdd6321e2ad6</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 21:21:14 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Clémence WALLER</dc:creator></item><item><category>Truth or Fake</category><title>November 17 blackout hoax: How a conspiracy theory went viral around the world</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/truth-or-fake/20261116-november-17-blackout-hoax-how-a-conspiracy-theory-went-viral-around-the-world</link><description>
A conspiracy theory claiming a worldwide “blackout” will hit on November 17 has spread across social media, cutting electricity, internet and banking services. The rumour stems from a routine US FEMA emergency alert test, but was amplified by cryptocurrency accounts, misleading claims about EU preparedness advice and references to The Simpsons. Recent technology outages, flight disruptions and cyberattacks have added to public anxiety, helping turn a routine test into a global blackout hoax. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4ad0d512-e1ff-11f1-9244-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/blackout.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4ad0d512-e1ff-11f1-9244-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/blackout.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5e88eb3a-e1ff-11f1-8f69-45b5e3a11287</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 20:50:29 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Vedika BAHL</dc:creator></item><item><category>Americas</category><title>Pope concludes South America homecoming, reassures faithful after cancer scare</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261116-pope-concludes-south-america-homecoming-reassures-faithful-after-cancer-scare</link><description>
Pope Leo XIV finished Monday his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru reiterating his advocacy for social justice, environmental protection and the importance of community. Just a month after undergoing lung cancer surgery, the 71-year-old pontiff drew millions of faithful across South America, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Mon, 16 Nov 2026 21:34:36 +0000 en <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message ]]>

On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.

They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster. The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA.

It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

Why it mattered

The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute.

"The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's."

The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University.

The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI.

As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13.

The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also beamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008.

]]> <![CDATA[ Relive Starship’s historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and ‘Mechazilla’ tower catch ]]> STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time.

Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable.

Liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did.

Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench.

The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies.

Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II, with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away.

EOS R5 Mark II: $3999
This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling.

Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review. View Deal

A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space, while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase.

That return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase.

Super heavy performed its landing burn above the Gulf of Mexico before cutting its engines for a brief moment and exploding in a giant fireball.

This was an intentional detonation, courtesy of the vehicle's flight termination system.

Ship continued on to low Earth orbit, where it deployed a payload of 26 upgraded Starlink Version 3 satellites. It was the second batch of V3 Starlinks delivered during Starship’s recent flight tests, each of which has added what SpaceX says is the equivalent of 10 Falcon 9 Starlink V2 satellite launches worth of data capacity to its orbital constellation.

Flight 15 was also Starship's second-ever mission to orbit, and its longest so far. Ship spent nearly a full day in orbit, circling Earth a total of 14 times. During its jaunt in space, the spacecraft cleared three separate check points, which allowed SpaceX the opportunity to divert the vehicle for an ocean splashdown if needed, and finally was given the green light to attempt the first-ever Ship tower catch.

At approximately 4:18 p.m. EST (2018 GMT, 3:18 p.m. local time in Texas) on Saturday (Nov. 14), the spacecraft broke through the cloud cover that blanketed the skies above Starbase as onlookers watched its bellyflop plunge toward the ground. Moments after becoming visible, Ship ignited its engines for a flip and burn maneuver, which oriented it upright and swung its trajectory into the tightening grip of the chopstick arms of Starbase's "Mechazilla" launch tower.

After a slight sway back and forth suspended above Earth in Mechazilla's embrace, Ship came to a complete rest, hanging motionless as a historic milestone in SpaceX’s pursuit of fully reusable spaceflight.

It hung there overnight as engineers, and even SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, inspected the spacecraft. Ship was lowered on Sunday (Nov. 15) and transported back to SpaceX's Starbase hanger bay for further checkouts.

SpaceX has not yet said whether Ship 42 will fly again, but its return gives engineers a chance to examine how the spacecraft held up through launch, nearly a day in orbit and atmospheric reentry.

Those findings will help inform upcoming flights as SpaceX ramps up production to continue testing Starship's capabilities.

]]> <![CDATA[ Elon Musk says SpaceX’s Starship, already the largest rocket on Earth, will get even bigger with next-gen V4 model ]]> As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big.

The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower.

It was a huge moment for SpaceX, bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship.

"Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15). "Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher-thrust V4 engines."

The current version of Starship — the one that launched Friday (Nov. 13) on the vehicle's 15th test flight — is the V3. It's the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 m) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage.

When is the best time to look for Leonid meteors?

The best time to spot Leonids is in the hours before dawn on Nov. 18, when the radiant will reach its highest point in the southeastern sky, maximizing the amount of meteors that may be seen skimming through Earth's atmosphere. By then, the waxing moon will have set, leaving darker skies and a better chance of spotting fainter meteors.

Shooting stars that appear close to the radiant will strike Earth almost head-on, leaving the shortest trails. Instead, find a patch of sky a short distance away from the constellation Leo, where the meteors will be at their most impressive, and give your eyes 20-30 minutes to fully adapt to the dark.

Why are the Leonids special?

As if shooting stars weren't enough, the Leonid shower is also known for spawning dazzling fireballs and long-lasting Earth-grazing meteors, which strike our atmosphere at an oblique angle, leaving long trains as they skim through before passing back out into space.

The shower is also capable of producing magnificent meteor storms when Earth passes through particularly dense trails of debris left behind by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. ]]> <![CDATA[ Could there be an ancient alien satellite in Earth's orbit? How the 'Black Knight' conspiracy theory has survived for over 100 years ]]> In the final days of 1998, as astronauts aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Endeavor were working during one of the early missions to assemble the International Space Station, crew members from the STS-88 mission captured photographs of a dark colored, unusually shaped object drifting through space.

Despite its unusual appearance in the photographs, the object had a conventional explanation, and one that was known to the astronauts at that time: it was one of several thermal covers that had been wrapped around trunnion pins used in the space station's construction. Upon noticing the "escape" of one of the covers, Mission Commander Bob Cabana remarked over the radio to fellow astronaut Jerry Ross that "one of the thermal covers got away from you."

Seeing the cover drifting away, a frustrated Ross snapped a photograph of it. Yet despite the innocuous story behind the images, they have nonetheless helped fuel belief in an unusual Space Age conspiracy theory: one involving the alleged presence of an ancient satellite, presumably of alien origin, that has long been orbiting our planet — perhaps since the end of the last Ice Age.

According to proponents of this theory, the object photographed by Ross in 1998 is actually what many call the "Black Knight Satellite," and is only one piece of evidence they point to in a long succession of unrelated — and often misinterpreted — events in modern history that supposedly lend further evidence to the alleged alien spacecraft's existence.

So how did such a legend gain traction in the first place, with some versions alleging that NASA and the U.S. government have worked to conceal evidence of the alleged space object's existence from the public?

Odd detections at Colorado Springs

Depending on which version of the story you come across, the strange roots of the Black Knight conspiracy theory might be traced all the way back to the nineteenth century, when the famous inventor Nikola Tesla began detecting unusual electrical signals while conducting radio experiments at his laboratory in Colorado Springs.

At the time, Tesla considered whether the signals might be communications from intelligent aliens on nearby planets, although the likely source had actually been terrestrial radio interference. Notably, Tesla also never claimed that the emissions might be coming from an object in Earth's orbit; nonetheless, some proponents of the Black Knight Satellite theories have incorporated Tesla's experiments into the mythos, suggesting they may represent some of the earliest detections of a mysterious object lurking near Earth.

Unidentified objects in orbit?

Another component that was later incorporated into the Black Knight Satellite mythos came to light in May 1954, when newspaper reports began publicizing author Donald Keyhoe's assertions that the U.S. Air Force had detected at least two unidentified satellites orbiting Earth.

At the time, Keyhoe claimed that U.S. government scientists at White Sands were reportedly "making an intensive effort to locate and chart the course of the satellites in an attempt to determine what they are and where they came from," as the author was quoted as saying in articles like one that appeared in the St. Louis Post-Dispatch on Friday, May 14, 1954.

However, later in August of that year, U.S. officials apparently concluded these objects were likely to have been meteors that became "satellites of the Earth and were revolving with it 400 to 600 miles out in space," and that Dr. Lincoln LaPaz, one of the preeminent experts on meteors at the time, had "definitely identified the objects as natural rather than man-made," as reported by the New York Times.

Just a few years later in February 1960, a similar story appeared in Time magazine, which this time alleged that the U.S. Navy had spotted an unidentified dark object in orbit that was suspected of being a Soviet reconnaissance satellite. This object was later identified as well, with officials determining it had likely been debris from the American spy satellite Discoverer 8.

Another similar claim suggests that on May 15, 1963, during the Mercury-Atlas 9 mission, NASA astronaut Gordon Cooper allegedly observed an unusual object in space, which some accounts describe as a "glowing green object" that followed his capsule. While it is true that Cooper reported seeing what he characterized as "John’s fireflies," which were a reference to earlier sightings of unusual luminous objects made by astronaut John Glenn during the Mercury-Atlas 6 mission, it was later concluded that the so-called "fireflies" resulted from small bits of ice separating from the spacecraft itself, which present a greenish hue as sunlight reflects off of them (audio of Cooper describing this during the Mercury-Atlas 9 mission can be found here).

Beyond this, however, there is no evidence of Cooper observing any singular object during this mission, either in Cooper's personal records or mission audio and transcripts from the time.

Arguably, one of the most extraordinary components of the Black Knight Satellite theory involves its alleged age, which according to some theories places its initial entry into Earth's orbit as far back as 13,000 years ago. But if so, how would anyone know this, and what evidence could support such an idea?

Understanding this bizarre aspect of the Black Knight mythos requires a look back at the theories of Scottish writer Duncan Lunan, which he first proposed in 1973. At that time, Lunan was receiving international attention for his investigation into mysterious long-delayed echoes, proposing that one theory behind the phenomenon could be that they represented signals from Earth that were being rebroadcast from an extraterrestrial probe — an idea that borrowed from theories first proposed by Australian scientist Ronald Bracewell.

According to Lunan's theory, such a hypothetical "Bracewell probe" might have arrived in Earth's vicinity roughly 13,000 years ago after traveling from within a planetary system associated with the star Epsilon Boötis, some 236 light-years away.

Within just a few years, Lunan had withdrawn his conclusions, but this did little to prevent his initial ideas about a 13,000-year-old alien satellite from being incorporated into the growing mythos surrounding the alleged Black Knight Satellite.

The STS-88 mission photographs

That brings us back to what are arguably the most widely circulated images associated with the Black Knight satellite: the famous images from NASA's STS-88 mission taken by astronaut Jerry Ross in December 1998.

According to spaceflight historian James Oberg, the object in Ross's photos could indeed be positively identified as the thermal blanket lost during the mission, especially since he had specifically asked Ross about the incident — and later misinterpretations of his photos as being evidence of an alien spacecraft — during an October 2014 interview.

At that time, Oberg asked Ross whether he had time during the 1998 spacewalk "to gaze at [the thermal cover] and think about how it looked," to which Ross said no, admitting he had been "too pissed at myself to wonder what it looked like!"

When asked what advice he would offer to those who have misinterpreted the object in his photographs for being something more exotic and otherworldly, Ross told Oberg, "If we see something up there we will be the first ones to ask questions and to tell people we saw something we didn't understand."

"Conspiracy theories are fun for those working on them, but a waste of valuable brain power," Ross added.

But what, specifically, about the idea of an ancient extraterrestrial probe lurking in orbit around our planet makes this far-fetched theory so captivating?

"I think it's because this idea of an alien satellite kicking around in orbit checks so many conspiracy theory boxes," says Amy Shira Teitel, a spaceflight historian who has also tackled the Black Knight satellite theories in the past, and points to other misperceptions about space that have given rise to conspiracy theories over the years.

"People, for some reason, believe space is fake or that every mission is fake because the Van Allen Belts will kill you," Shira Teitel recently told Space in an email, while noting that most missions take place well within safe distances from the inner radiation belt, with notable exceptions that include the Gemini 11 mission, as well as lunar flights.

"People also love UFOs," she adds. "Even skeptics have a little bit of a soft spot for the idea of an alien craft flying by to say hi. I think when you take all these conspiracy threads together, the Black Knight sort of fits perfectly in that intersection!"

Overall, the bizarre story of the Black Knight satellite offers a textbook example of how a collection of unconnected events and speculative interpretations can gradually accumulate into a single narrative over time.

Despite this reality, belief in the existence of a mysterious ancient satellite lurking in orbit will likely persist for years to come, helping ensure its place as one of the most peculiar — and enduring — legends of the Space Age.

Upon noticing the "escape" of one of the covers, Mission Commander Bob Cabana remarked over the radio to fellow astronaut Jerry Ross that "one of the thermal covers got away from you."

Seeing the cover drifting away, a frustrated Ross snapped a photograph of it. Yet despite the innocuous story behind the images, they have nonetheless helped fuel belief in an unusual Space Age conspiracy theory: one involving the alleged presence of an ancient satellite, presumably of alien origin, that has long been orbiting our planet — perhaps since the end of the last Ice Age.

According to proponents of this theory, the object photographed by Ross in 1998 is actually what many call the "Black Knight Satellite," and is only one piece of evidence they point to in a long succession of unrelated — and often misinterpreted — events in modern history that supposedly lend further evidence to the alleged alien spacecraft's existence.

So how did such a legend gain traction in the first place, with some versions alleging that NASA and the U.S. government have worked to conceal evidence of the alleged space object's existence from the public?

Odd detections at Colorado Springs

Depending on which version of the story you come across, the strange roots of the Black Knight conspiracy theory might be traced all the way back to the nineteenth century, when the famous inventor Nikola Tesla began detecting unusual electrical signals while conducting radio experiments at his laboratory in Colorado Springs.

At the time, Tesla considered whether the signals might be communications from intelligent aliens on nearby planets, although the likely source had actually been terrestrial radio interference. Notably, Tesla also never claimed that the emissions might be coming from an object in Earth's orbit; nonetheless, some proponents of the Black Knight Satellite theories have incorporated Tesla's experiments into the mythos, suggesting they may represent some of the earliest detections of a mysterious object lurking near Earth.

Unidentified objects in orbit?

Another component that was later incorporated into the Black Knight Satellite mythos came to light in May 1954, when newspaper reports began publicizing author Donald Keyhoe's assertions that the U.S. Air Force had detected at least two unidentified satellites orbiting Earth.

At the time, Keyhoe claimed that U.S. government scientists at White Sands were reportedly "making an intensive effort to locate and chart the course of the satellites in an attempt to determine what they are and where they came from," as the author was quoted as saying in articles like one that appeared in the St. Louis Post-Dispatch on Friday, May 14, 1954.

However, later in August of that year, U.S. officials apparently concluded these objects were likely to have been meteors that became "satellites of the Earth and were revolving with it 400 to 600 miles out in space," and that Dr. Lincoln LaPaz, one of the preeminent experts on meteors at the time, had "definitely identified the objects as natural rather than man-made," as reported by the New York Times.

Just a few years later in February 1960, a similar story appeared in Time magazine, which this time alleged that the U.S. Navy had spotted an unidentified dark object in orbit that was suspected of being a Soviet reconnaissance satellite. This object was later identified as well, with officials determining it had likely been debris from the American spy satellite Discoverer 8.

Another similar claim suggests that on May 15, 1963, during the Mercury-Atlas 9 mission, NASA astronaut Gordon Cooper allegedly observed an unusual object in space, which some accounts describe as a "glowing green object" that followed his capsule. While it is true that Cooper reported seeing what he characterized as "John’s fireflies," which were a reference to earlier sightings of unusual luminous objects made by astronaut John Glenn during the Mercury-Atlas 6 mission, it was later concluded that the so-called "fireflies" resulted from small bits of ice separating from the spacecraft itself, which present a greenish hue as sunlight reflects off of them (audio of Cooper describing this during the Mercury-Atlas 9 mission can be found here).

Beyond this, however, there is no evidence of Cooper observing any singular object during this mission, either in Cooper's personal records or mission audio and transcripts from the time.

"Echoes" from a 13,000-year-old satellite

Arguably, one of the most extraordinary components of the Black Knight Satellite theory involves its alleged age, which according to some theories places its initial entry into Earth's orbit as far back as 13,000 years ago. But if so, how would anyone know this, and what evidence could support such an idea?

Understanding this bizarre aspect of the Black Knight mythos requires a look back at the theories of Scottish writer Duncan Lunan, which he first proposed in 1973. At that time, Lunan was receiving international attention for his investigation into mysterious long-delayed echoes, proposing that one theory behind the phenomenon could be that they represented signals from Earth that were being rebroadcast from an extraterrestrial probe — an idea that borrowed from theories first proposed by Australian scientist Ronald Bracewell.

According to Lunan's theory, such a hypothetical "Bracewell probe" might have arrived in Earth's vicinity roughly 13,000 years ago after traveling from within a planetary system associated with the star Epsilon Boötis, some 236 light-years away.

Within just a few years, Lunan had withdrawn his conclusions, but this did little to prevent his initial ideas about a 13,000-year-old alien satellite from being incorporated into the growing mythos surrounding the alleged Black Knight Satellite.

The STS-88 mission photographs

That brings us back to what are arguably the most widely circulated images associated with the Black Knight satellite: the famous images from NASA's STS-88 mission taken by astronaut Jerry Ross in December 1998.

According to spaceflight historian James Oberg, the object in Ross's photos could indeed be positively identified as the thermal blanket lost during the mission, especially since he had specifically asked Ross about the incident — and later misinterpretations of his photos as being evidence of an alien spacecraft — during an October 2014 interview.

At that time, Oberg asked Ross whether he had time during the 1998 spacewalk "to gaze at [the thermal cover] and think about how it looked," to which Ross said no, admitting he had been "too pissed at myself to wonder what it looked like!"

When asked what advice he would offer to those who have misinterpreted the object in his photographs for being something more exotic and otherworldly, Ross told Oberg, "If we see something up there we will be the first ones to ask questions and to tell people we saw something we didn't understand."

"Conspiracy theories are fun for those working on them, but a waste of valuable brain power," Ross added.

The legend continues

But what, specifically, about the idea of an ancient extraterrestrial probe lurking in orbit around our planet makes this far-fetched theory so captivating?

"I think it's because this idea of an alien satellite kicking around in orbit checks so many conspiracy theory boxes," says Amy Shira Teitel, a spaceflight historian who has also tackled the Black Knight satellite theories in the past, and points to other misperceptions about space that have given rise to conspiracy theories over the years.

"People, for some reason, believe space is fake or that every mission is fake because the Van Allen Belts will kill you," Shira Teitel recently told Space in an email, while noting that most missions take place well within safe distances from the inner radiation belt, with notable exceptions that include the Gemini 11 mission, as well as lunar flights.

"People also love UFOs," she adds. "Even skeptics have a little bit of a soft spot for the idea of an alien craft flying by to say hi. I think when you take all these conspiracy threads together, the Black Knight sort of fits perfectly in that intersection!"

Overall, the bizarre story of the Black Knight satellite offers a textbook example of how a collection of unconnected events and speculative interpretations can gradually accumulate into a single narrative over time.

Despite this reality, belief in the existence of a mysterious ancient satellite lurking in orbit will likely persist for years to come, helping ensure its place as one of the most peculiar — and enduring — legends of the Space Age.

   <title>Odchod Šmuclera? Kolegové oceňují práci doma i ve světě, kritika míří na sítě</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/zdravotnictvi/roman-smucler-rezignace-reakce/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zdravotnictvi</link>
   <description>Byl vidět a pro obor stomatologie toho hodně udělal, což vyvrcholilo konáním Světového stomatologického kongresu FDI v Praze. Tak kolegové z řad zubních lékařů hodnotí bezmála desetileté působení Romana Šmuclera v čele České stomatologické komory. Respekt si získal i u lidí mimo zubní lékařství. Na víkendovém sněmu komory v Brně ale její představenstvo, kvůli výhradám týkajícím se vzájemné spolupráce, navrhlo zařadit bod k jeho odvolání. Šmucler na funkci posléze sám rezignoval.</description>
   <pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:30:00 +0100</pubDate>

    <media:description>Prezident České stomatologické komory Roman Šmucler (na snímku ze 4. září 2026) rezignoval. Představenstvo navrhovalo jeho odvolání. V čele komory byl Šmucler od roku 2017.</media:description>

Jakub Mencl vystřídal Jitku Volfovou</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905964-ceska-lipa-ma-noveho-starostu-jakub-mencl-vystridal-jitku-volfovou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905964-ceska-lipa-ma-noveho-starostu-jakub-mencl-vystridal-jitku-volfovou.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 19:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Česká Lípa má oficiálně osmého porevolučního starostu. Mladá řidička předjížděla přes plnou čáru</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905959-vazna-nehoda-u-pertoltic-mlada-ridicka-predjizdela-pres-plnou-caru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905959-vazna-nehoda-u-pertoltic-mlada-ridicka-predjizdela-pres-plnou-caru.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:39:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Středně těžké poranění si vyžádala dopravní nehoda, ke které došlo v pondělí před polednem v katastru Pertoltic. Mladá řidička na silnici 270 mezi Jablonným a Mimoní předjížděla na úseku s plnou čárou a auto několikrát přetočila přes střechu.</description></item><item><title>V úterý je svátek. Jak to bude 17. listopadu s nákupy?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905875-zitra-je-svatek-jak-to-bude-17-listopadu-s-nakupy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905875-zitra-je-svatek-jak-to-bude-17-listopadu-s-nakupy.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Markéta Hamerníková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Úterní státní svátek přináší i praktickou otázku: bude kde nakoupit? Rozhodující není samotný svátek, ale to, zda ho zákon zahrnuje mezi dny se zákazem prodeje.</description></item><item><title>Liberec dnes zahájil provoz první linky poptávkové dopravy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905901-liberec-dnes-zahajil-provoz-prvni-linky-poptavkove-dopravy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905901-liberec-dnes-zahajil-provoz-prvni-linky-poptavkove-dopravy.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Dopravní podnik v Liberci (DPMLJ) dnes zahájil provoz první linky poptávkové dopravy, kdy vozidlo MHD přijede na objednání. Ten brzy skončí</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905588-ustecku-pomohly-stovky-projektu-z-fondu-spravedlive-transformace-ten-brzy-skonci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905588-ustecku-pomohly-stovky-projektu-z-fondu-spravedlive-transformace-ten-brzy-skonci.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:57:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Téměř 16 miliard korun čerpal Ústecký kraj v posledních letech z Fondu spravedlivé transformace. Ten v Česku podporoval regiony dotčené těžbou uhlí. Jenže fond brzy končí. Co bude dál? A co vlastně peníze regionu přinesly? O tom se debatovalo v Ústí nad Labem.</description></item><item><title>Týden proprší, na horách bude sněžit</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905877-tyden-proprsi-na-horach-bude-snezit.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905877-tyden-proprsi-na-horach-bude-snezit.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Nový pracovní týden bude podle předpovědi meteorologů spíše deštivý, ve vyšších polohách se pak objeví sněžení. Občas se ale může objevit i slunce.</description></item><item><title>Tragická nehoda u Svoru. Auto narazilo do stromu, jeden člověk zemřel</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905880-tragicka-nehoda-u-svoru-auto-narazilo-do-stromu-jeden-clovek-zemrel.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905880-tragicka-nehoda-u-svoru-auto-narazilo-do-stromu-jeden-clovek-zemrel.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:23:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Na silnici I/9 u Svoru na Českolipsku bouralo v noci osobní auto, které ze zatím neznámých důvodů vyjelo ze silnice a narazilo do stromu. Tragická nehoda stála život jednoho ze spolujezdců, další tři lidé utrpěli zranění a skončili v liberecké nemocnici.</description></item><item><title>Příprava opravy Svijanské arény v Liberci se komplikuje, rozhodne nové vedení města</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905850-priprava-opravy-svijanske-areny-v-liberci-se-komplikuje-rozhodne-nove.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905850-priprava-opravy-svijanske-areny-v-liberci-se-komplikuje-rozhodne-nove.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 06:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Příprava opravy zchátralé střechy zimního stadionu Svijanská aréna v městském Sport parku v Liberci se komplikuje. Shodně gólem a asistencí se se na triumfu domácích podíleli útočníci Adam Najman a Jakub Rychlovský.</description></item><item><title>Ovečky opustily svahy Ještědu. Na zimu se přestěhovaly do nového zázemí ve Vesci</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905851-ovecky-opustily-svahy-jestedu-na-zimu-se-prestehovaly-do-noveho-zazemi-ve-vesci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905851-ovecky-opustily-svahy-jestedu-na-zimu-se-prestehovaly-do-noveho-zazemi-ve-vesci.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 18:29:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Stádo deseti ovcí, které od června spásalo sjezdovku Skalka na Ještědu, se dnes přestěhovalo na zimní pobyt do libereckého Vesce. Podle Městských lesů Liberec nyní horské louky předávají štafetu lyžařům. Zvířata mají v novém působišti u Tajchu připravené útulné zázemí i krmný zvon plný sena.</description></item></channel></rss>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:12:33 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.4 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Starostovník 2026 https://www.vybezek.eu/295747-starostovnik-2026/ Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:41:02 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295747 V termínu 9. a 10. října 2026 proběhly další komunální (a senátní) volby, Tudíž je čas na aktualizaci – snad už mají všichni na svých webech všechno správně.

Vlastně je to obdivuhodné (nebo spíš pozoruhodné?). Někde vážně stačí postavit jednu jedinou kandidátku a všechno je OK. Někde ostřílení matadoři zmizeli v propadlišti dějin a došlo k totální proměně. Někde opakují stále stejné chyby. Ale hlavně – pořád zůstává faktem, že spousta nespokojených a nadávajících nedokáže zvednout pozadí a zkusit cokoli dělat. Víte, že aby místní referendum bylo platné, musí se jej zúčastnit alespoň 35 %?

Dolní Podluží –

Dolní Podluží na FB:

DOLNÍ PODLUŽÍ MÁ NOVÉ VEDENÍ OBCE
Dnes proběhlo ustavující zasedání Zastupitelstva obce Dolní Podluží pro volební období 2026–2030.
Starostou obce byl zvolen pan Vít Nesnídal a místostarostou pan Jan Hampl.
Nově zvolenému vedení obce i všem členům zastupitelstva přejeme mnoho úspěchů, vzájemné spolupráce a správných rozhodnutí ve prospěch naší obce a jejích obyvatel.
Ať se Dolnímu Podluží daří i v dalších letech!

Jiříkov –

Město Jiříkov na FB:

NOVÉ ZASTUPITELSTVO JIŘÍKOVA ZAHÁJILO SVÉ VOLEBNÍ OBDOBÍ
(Jiříkovské noviny listopad 2026)
V pondělí 9. 11. 2026 se uskutečnilo ustavující zasedání Zastupitelstva města Jiříkov, které zahájilo nové čtyřleté volební období 2026–2030. Na programu bylo především složení slibu nově zvolených zastupitelů, volba vedení města a dalších orgánů samosprávy.
Po složení zákonem předepsaného slibu přistoupili zastupitelé k volbě starosty a místostarosty města. Starostou Jiříkova byl zvolen a svou funkci tak obhájil Ing. Bc. Jindřich Jurajda, DiS. (NEZÁVISLÍ KANDIDÁTI MĚSTA JIŘÍKOVA), který tak bude město zastupovat a řídit v dalších čtyřech letech. Funkci místostarosty bude nově vykonávat Ludvík Otradovský (Jiříkov 2030 – sportovci / hasiči / ODS).
Zastupitelstvo dále zvolilo členy Rady města Jiříkov. Jejími členy se stali Mgr. Michal Mrázek a Jaroslav Vöröš (NEZÁVISLÍ KANDIDÁTI MĚSTA JIŘÍKOVA) a Ing. Nikol Kopecká (Spolek přátel Jiříkova a Filipova). Součástí jednání byla také volba předsedů a členů finančního a kontrolního výboru. V čele finančního výboru usedla stejně jako v minulém volebním období Naděžda Stožická (NEZÁVISLÍ KANDIDÁTI MĚSTA JIŘÍKOVA) a předsedou kontrolního výboru se stal Mgr. Petr Kulhánek MBA (ANO 2011).
Nově zvolené vedení města tak přebírá odpovědnost za další rozvoj Jiříkova, hospodaření s městským majetkem, přípravu a realizaci investičních projektů i každodenní chod městské samosprávy.
Nové zastupitelstvo tvoří celkem 15 členů zvolených za čtyři kandidující uskupení. Jejich společným úkolem bude rozhodovat o důležitých otázkách života města a zastupovat zájmy jeho obyvatel.
Všem nově zvoleným zastupitelům přejeme hodně sil, trpělivosti a úspěchů při práci pro Jiříkov a jeho občany.

Na FB:

Krásná Lípa zvolila vedení města pro nové volební období

Dnes v podvečer proběhlo ustavující zasedání Zastupitelstva města Krásná Lípa. Do čela města bylo opět zvoleno dosavadní vedení. Starostou se stal Jan Kolář, první místostarostkou Jana Drobečková a druhým, neuvolněným místostarostou Zbyněk Linhart. V sedmičlenné radě města je doplní Karel Jarolímek, Jiří Podhorský, Jakub Melichar a Marek Simandl.

Nové volební období tak začíná ve znamení kontinuity a stability, s možností navázat na dosavadní práci a pokračovat v připravených projektech pro další rozvoj, ve prospěch města a jeho obyvatel.

Varnsdorfský minitrh? Za nás rozhodně povedená sobota!

Včera jsme vyrazili do Městské knihovny ve Varnsdorfu a rozhodně jsme tam nebyli jen do počtu! Roman představil svou už třetí pohádkovou knížku Mokré pohádky a my jsme s sebou přivezli také kousek našeho Život jde dál. Výrobky, na kterých se podíleli nevidomí a slabozrací, spoustu věcí k vidění i k zakoupení a hlavně chuť potkávat se s lidmi.

A že se jich u nás zastavilo! Někdo nakoupil, někdo si přišel popovídat, někdo nás podpořil jen svou přítomností. A přesně o tom to je. Každá taková podpora se počítá a každé milé setkání potěší.

Obrovské díky naší babče, Vlaďce Hermanové a Renatě Šimákové, které nám s tím vším pomáhaly. A samozřejmě děkujeme paní ředitelce za pozvání, milé přijetí a atmosféru, ve které se člověk cítí jako mezi svými.

Děkujeme všem, kteří za námi přišli, podpořili nás a udělali si čas. Bylo nám s vámi krásně!

Visit Varnsdorf:

Náš kraj má co vyprávět. A Regionální knižní minitrh to znovu potvrdil.

Za každou knihou je příběh. Za každým rukodělným výrobkem hodiny práce, nápadů a šikovných rukou. A za každou uchovanou tradicí člověk, kterému záleží na tom, aby nezmizela.

Právě takové bylo sobotní setkání s lidmi, kteří mají co říct, co předat a především chuť tvořit. S autory, kteří vydávají knihy a uchovávají příběhy našeho regionu. S tvůrci a řemeslníky, kteří vlastníma rukama vyrábějí originální věci, navazují na tradice a dávají jim nový život. Právě jejich práce, nápady a nadšení pomáhají udržovat místní kulturu živou a připomínají, jak bohatý a inspirativní náš kraj je.

Velké poděkování patří všem, kteří se na minitrhu představili. Ať už prostřednictvím svých knih, rukodělných výrobků, poctivé řemeslné práce nebo osobního příběhu. Děkujeme, že svou tvorbou obohacujete náš region a pomáháte uchovávat jeho jedinečnost pro další generace.

Poděkování si zaslouží také Městská knihovna Varnsdorf a celý její tým za skvělou přípravu, organizaci a příjemnou atmosféru, díky které se knihovna na jeden den proměnila v místo plné setkávání, inspirace a objevování.

A právě takové setkání má smysl.
